research_rationale: Read the held Federal Register text of EO 14373 (91 FR 2045 to 2047, January 15, 2026; jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_14373.txt) in full. The order finds that attachment or other judicial process against the Foreign Government Deposit Funds (Venezuelan government funds held in designated Treasury accounts) would harm national security and foreign policy, declares a national emergency under IEEPA and the NEA (Section 1), defines the funds (Section 2), voids and prohibits attachment and unlicensed dealing and overrides earlier orders to the extent they affect the funds (Section 3), records further findings (Section 4), directs the Secretaries of the Treasury and State and the Attorney General on custody, disbursement and assertion of immunity (Section 5), authorizes rulemaking, agency implementation and congressional reports (Section 6) and states general provisions (Section 7). The prepared inventory of 28 clauses matches the text and is confirmed. The order has no duration or sunset; its only timing words are the effective-date reference in Section 3(b) and the publication-cost provision in Section 7(d). The three bounded machine searches were read (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, Office of the Federal Register disposition notes) and return zero hits, so no amendment, revocation or supersession is shown. The held-corpus search for the order number finds only the Federal Register copy of the order and two Office of Foreign Assets Control notices of September 30, 2026 (91 FR, issue 188) publishing general licenses that refer to the Foreign Government Deposit Funds as specified in the order; they are implementing licences issued under Section 3 and are leads, not relied on as a legal basis. Because the national emergency was declared on January 9, 2026, its first anniversary (January 9, 2027) falls after the 2026-10-14 cutoff, so no National Emergencies Act continuation notice was due or could yet exist; the claim relies on the statutory one-year term of a declared emergency unless terminated earlier, whose text is not separately held, and no termination is shown. Twenty-seven clauses are therefore operative on 2026-10-14 under the held original plus bounded search route and Section 7(d) is spent by performance on publication. Limits: the U.S. Code search does not reflect laws enacted from 2026-10-10 through 2026-10-14; the National Emergencies Act text is not held and the one-year term is stated as law without a held copy.
savings_reason: EO 14373 has no savings or transitional provision; nothing in the held later materials ends or preserves any residual effect of the order.
earlier_end_check: Own terms: the order has no 'until', 'terminate', 'expire' or deadline language that ends a command; Section 7(d) is spent on publication. Later instruments: no held text and no disposition note amends, revokes or supersedes EO 14373, and the national emergency was not shown terminated, so no earlier end is established for any continuing clause.
scope_check: Complete operative inventory of 28 clauses as prepared: the ordering lead, Sections 1 to 7 with their paragraphs. Findings and determinations (Sections 1 and 4) are recorded as operative statements on which the Section 3 and 5 commands rest; they are not separate commands.
independent_command_check: Section 3 (prohibitions), Section 5 (custody and immunity directions to the Treasury and Justice), and Section 6 (rulemaking and reports) are independent commands, but all depend on the declared national emergency and the order itself and none has a separate end. Section 3(c)'s supersession of earlier orders is limited to the Foreign Government Deposit Funds.
savings_check: No savings clause is stated. Section 7(a) preserves authority granted by law and the functions of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget; it is a continuing provision, not a savings for an ended command.

research_rationale: Read the held Federal Register text of EO 10431 (18 FR 437, 3 CFR 1949-1953 Comp. p. 927; jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10431.txt) in full. It establishes the National Security Medal and has an ordering lead and six numbered items. The prepared inventory omitted item 4 because the OCR reads its number as '4 -', so the inventory is corrected by characters to seven clauses (lead and items 1 to 6). The held Federal Register text of Executive Order 13709 (80 FR 60793, October 7, 2015) is the only later instrument found: section 1(a) rewrites item 2, section 1(b) adds items 7 and 8, and section 2 supersedes the 1953 regulations published with the order; none of them revokes or supersedes the order itself. The three bounded machine searches (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, Office of the Federal Register disposition notes) were read; their hits for this order are leads (the Executive Order 13709 amendment and later citations) and no instrument is shown ending the order. The held-corpus number search finds the order, its 1989 codification SOURCE line, the American Presidency Project and Federal Register copies of Executive Order 13709. Every item is therefore operative on 2026-10-14 under the held original plus bounded search route, item 2 as amended. Limits: the U.S. Code search does not reflect laws enacted from 2026-10-10 through 2026-10-14; the text is the OCR layer of the official page.
savings_reason: EO 10431 has no savings or transitional provision. Medals already awarded under it are not undone by any held later instrument; Executive Order 13709 changes eligibility prospectively only in its own terms.
conflict_resolutions: {"PARTIAL_END_CANDIDATE_ON_YES_ORDER":"The three supersession candidates all come from section 2 of Executive Order 13709, which supersedes the regulations governing the award of the National Security Medal that were issued with Presidential approval on January 19, 1953 and published with Executive Order 10431. Those regulations are a separate implementing text, not one of the order's seven clauses, and the section does not say that it revokes or supersedes Executive Order 10431 or any of its items; the same order's section 1 amends item 2 and adds items 7 and 8 of Executive Order 10431, which presupposes that the order continues. No clause is therefore ended; item 2 is recorded as amended and item 3 discloses the supersession of the regulations it refers to."}

The U.S. Code search does not reflect laws enacted from 2026-10-10 through 2026-10-14.

The three bounded machine searches were read (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, Office of the Federal Register disposition notes) and show no instrument ending the order. The abolition is spent by performance on issuance, and the amendment is operative on 2026-10-14. Limits: the U.S. Code search does not reflect laws enacted from 2026-10-10 through 2026-10-14; the 5 CFR sentence is a lead and is not relied on as a legal basis.
